thought.text: While pnpm installs, let me check PostgreSQL 15 availability:

reasoning_content:
Alright, let's install PostgreSQL 15 + PostGIS. Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy) has postgresql-15 in its standard repositories (Jammy ships with PG 14 by default, but PG 15 was added in the security updates — actually, Ubuntu 22.04's default is postgresql-14, and postgresql-15 is available in the universe repository for 22.04? Let's check. Actually, Jammy's main repository has postgresql-14. PG 15 is available in 22.04's universe from 22.04.3 onwards? Hmm.

The standard method: use the PostgreSQL APT repository (apt.postgresql.org). This has postgresql-15 and postgis 3 for all supported releases. Let's use this.

Actually, first let me check whether postgresql-15 is available in apt without adding the repository. I'll run `apt-cache policy postgresql-15 postgis-15` or search for it.

action.command: apt-cache policy postgresql-15 postgresql-14 postgis 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 "^[a-z]" | head -12

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "apt-cache policy postgresql-15 postgresql-14 postgis 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 \"^[a-z]\" | head -12", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Check PostgreSQL versions in apt"}
